newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall 1.95 pct on fears of SEBI rules.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall 1.95 pct on fears of SEBI rules.

text.p: Delhi shares ended sharply lower on Wednesday as speculators sold on fears that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) might introduce uniform settlement operations at all bourses, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 15.38 points, nearly two percent, lower at 773.05.

"Fears that SEBI might ask stock exchange authorities to bring uniform trading settlement made speculators offload the positions they had created in early trade," said Ajit S. Sial of brokers Sial and Company.
"In case of uniformity in settlement on the bourses the operators will not be able to create speculative positions," Sial added.
SEBI was due to hold a meeting in Bombay later on Wednesday.
Brokers said shares of Smithkline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd continued to be in demand following the announcement of a bonus share issue by the company.
Smithkline Beecham, which on Tuesday offered a bonus of three shares for every five shares held, rose 6.0 rupees, or two percent, to 306, brokers said.
Reliance Industries fell 11.25 rupees to 281 on selling by speculators and financial institutions, brokers said.
TISCO lost 5.95 rupees to 183 on late selling by speculators.
State Bank of India dropped 10.55 rupees to 310.
Larsen and Toubro quoted 6.05 rupees lower at 228.45.
